table_headers: 6.4.1 Safety Criteria for Adjustment of Stopping Doses

Dose administration at the current level or dose-escalation will be terminated if either of the following are observed: · There are 2 similar SAEs or clinically significant AEs within the same cohort. · There are 3 or more similar AEs in this study that are deemed a medically unacceptable risk by the Investigator, the DSMB and the Sponsor.

The following stopping rules will be applied: . Occurrence of any Death · Occurrence of two or more Grade 3 and above systemic adverse events (CTCAE v.5) · Occurrence of two or more ocular adverse events that do not resolve within 14 days. Dose administration at the current level or dose-escalation will be paused and re- evaluated by the DSMB, Principal Investigator and the Sponsor. Next steps will be further decided based on their recommendations
Per FDA comments added additional stopping rules 38

results.text: To assess the safety of a single unilateral subretinal administration of OCU410 in subjects with Geographic Atrophy (GA) secondary to dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD).

1. If none of the first 3 subjects on medium dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), then the dose will be escalated to high dose concentration for the next cohort.

2. If 2 or more of the first 3 subjects on medium dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

3. If exactly 1 of the first 3 subjects on medium dose concentration is determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then 3 additional subjects will be enrolled on medium dose concentration.

a) If none of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be escalated to high dose concentration for the next cohort.

b) If 1 or more of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

Cohort 3 High Dose (1.5x1011vg/mL): 3 subjects will receive a subretinal injection of 200 ul of OCU410 high dose concentration.

The DSMB will review two weeks safety data after dosing the first subject in cohort 3. If there are no dose-limiting toxicities observed, Phase 2 dosing will begin simultaneously with subsequent subjects in Cohort 3. In the event of a DLT, the algorithm of DLT (de-escalation or addition of 3 subjects) will be followed.

If a subject is diagnosed with wet AMD in the study eye or fellow eye at any point during the study, they will remain part of the study and must continue to follow the assessment schedule as outlined in the protocol.

5. Any ophthalmologic condition that reduces the clarity of the media and that, in the opinion of the Investigator, prevents adequate imaging of the retina and interferes with ophthalmologic examination (e.g., advanced cataract or corneal abnormalities).

6. Have hypersensitivity to fluorescein or any contradiction for subretinal injection.

7. Aphakia, Cataract surgery or any other intraocular surgery (including lens replacement surgery) within 3 months (prior to Screening), YAG capsulotomy within 1-month, and any ophthalmic condition that may require surgery during the study period.

8. History of uveitis or endophthalmitis or laser therapy in the macular region.

9. Considered unsuitable by the Investigator for any reason including medical or psychiatric that may either place the subject at increased risk during participation or interfere with the interpretation of the study outcomes after reviewing medical, ocular, and psychiatric history, clinical examination, and laboratory evaluation (i.e., ≥ 1.5 times upper limit normal [ULN] or > 2-fold elevation of serum creatinine, etc.)
